title: Cabbage Rose (Rosa Centifolia Simplex)
creator: Pierre-Joseph Redouté (French, 1759–1840)
attribution: Pierre-Joseph Redouté (French, 1759–1840), Cabbage Rose (Rosa Centifolia Simplex), 1817–24. The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift in the name of Warren H. Corning from his wife and children (1959.14). CC0 1.0.
notes: Rose pink Cabbage Rose, big open front-facing bloom on warm cream paper, strong saturated pink, clean outline. Cutout: easy (paper key), thorny stem and leaves separable.

title: Les Roses: Rosa Damascena, subalba
creator: Henri Joseph Redouté (French, 1766–1853)
attribution: Henri Joseph Redouté (French, 1766–1853), Les Roses:  Rosa Damascena, subalba, 1817–1824. The Cleveland Museum of Art, Mr. and Mrs. Charles G. Prasse Collection (1965.291). CC0 1.0.
notes: White Damask rose (Rosa damascena subalba), three white blooms with yellow centres seen front and three-quarter, grey-green leaves. Cutout: easy on pale paper but whites need edge care; keep caption area out.

title: The Roses: Rosa Gallica Purpurea Velutina Parva
creator: Langlois (French)
attribution: Langlois (French), The Roses:  Rosa Gallica Purpurea Velutina Parva, 1817–24. The Cleveland Museum of Art, Mr. and Mrs. Charles G. Prasse Collection (1965.293). CC0 1.0.
notes: Deep crimson-purple Gallica rose (Rosa gallica purpurea velutina), two full dark blooms three-quarter view plus bud, rich dark red that glows on a dark ground. Cutout: easy; dark petals against pale paper key cleanly.

title: Les Roses: Rosa Gallica
creator: Pierre-Joseph Redouté (French, 1759–1840)
attribution: Pierre-Joseph Redouté (French, 1759–1840), Les Roses:  Rosa Gallica, 1817–24. The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of The Print Club of Cleveland in honor of Mrs. William G. Mather (1955.471). CC0 1.0.
notes: Large blush double Gallica bloom, three-quarter view, soft pink-grey, tall stem with bud and big leaves. Cutout easy; low saturation, may need a rose re-tint.

title: The Roses: China or Bengal Rose
creator: Henri Joseph Redouté (French, 1766–1853)
attribution: Henri Joseph Redouté (French, 1766–1853), The Roses: China or Bengal Rose, 1817–24. The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of The Print Club of Cleveland, for the Donald Gray Memorial Collection (1943.138). CC0 1.0.
notes: Blush China rose, big open bloom plus several buds and a hip, plate has a plate-mark border and cream toned paper. Cutout: moderate (border must be cropped). Also usable for bloom stages.

title: Provence or French Rose
creator: Henri Joseph Redouté (French, 1766–1853)
attribution: Henri Joseph Redouté (French, 1766–1853), Provence or French Rose, 1817–1824. The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of The Print Club of Cleveland, for the Donald Gray Memorial Collection (1943.139). CC0 1.0.
notes: Deep red Provence rose (Rosa gallica), single crimson bloom front view with side buds, delicate foliage. Cutout easy.

title: Moss Rose
creator: Henri Joseph Redouté (French, 1766–1853)
attribution: Henri Joseph Redouté (French, 1766–1853), Moss Rose, 1817–1824. The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of The Print Club of Cleveland, for the Donald Gray Memorial Collection (1943.141). CC0 1.0.
notes: Moss rose with a mossy-sepal bud at top, half-open bud and open bloom on one thorny stem: stages in one plate. Cutout moderate (toned paper); bud and sepals are separable layers.

title: Pompon Rose
creator: Pierre-Joseph Redouté (French, 1759–1840)
attribution: Pierre-Joseph Redouté (French, 1759–1840), Pompon Rose, 1817–24. The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of The Print Club of Cleveland, for the Donald Gray Memorial Collection (1943.142). CC0 1.0.
notes: Pompon rose with tight buds, half-open and fully open blooms on one branch: three stages. Small flowers; plate high resolution. Cutout easy.

title: Moss rose (Rosa centifolia 'Muscosa'): flowering stem. Coloured zincograph, c. 1853, after M. Burnett.
creator: Burnett, M. A., active 1850.
attribution: Burnett, M. A., active 1850., Moss rose (Rosa centifolia 'Muscosa'): flowering stem. Coloured zincograph, c. 1853, after M. Burnett. [1853]. Wellcome Collection (Wellcome Collection), Public Domain Mark 1.0.
notes: Moss rose, one large full-open pink bloom plus a tight mossy bud top left, bright pink with dark leaves, coloured zincograph; stages bud and open on one stem. Cutout easy (grey-pink paper key).

title: Eglantine rose (Rosa eglanteria): flowering stem, fruit and floral segments. Coloured engraving after J. Sowerby, 1802.
creator: James Sowerby
attribution: James Sowerby, Eglantine rose (Rosa eglanteria): flowering stem, fruit and floral segments. Coloured engraving after J. Sowerby, 1802. 1 March 1802. Wellcome Collection (Wellcome Collection), Public Domain Mark 1.0.
notes: Eglantine rose: open flower, bud, hip and, bottom left, loose petal and sepal-like floral segments drawn separately; engraving partly coloured (left leaves are line only). Useful for single petals and the hip. Cutout moderate.

title: A wild rose (Rosa dumetorum): flowering and fruiting stems. Coloured engraving, c. 1829, after J. Sowerby.
creator: James Sowerby
attribution: James Sowerby, A wild rose (Rosa dumetorum): flowering and fruiting stems. Coloured engraving, c. 1829, after J. Sowerby. 1 November 1829. Wellcome Collection (Wellcome Collection), Public Domain Mark 1.0.
notes: Wild rose with thorny cane, big arching leaves and hip; partly coloured (lower leaves line only). Thorny cane is clean. Cutout moderate.

title: English ivy (Hedera helix): stem with flowers, fruit and leaves. Coloured lithograph by W. G. Smith, c. 1863, after himself.
creator: Worthington George Smith
attribution: Worthington George Smith, English ivy (Hedera helix): stem with flowers, fruit and leaves. Coloured lithograph by W. G. Smith, c. 1863, after himself. [1863-1880]. Wellcome Collection (Wellcome Collection), Public Domain Mark 1.0.
notes: Common ivy (Hedera helix), stem with flower cluster, fruit and leaves in dark green on white paper, coloured lithograph. Cutout easy; one of the cleanest candidates.

title: Granadilla or passion flower (Passiflora quadrangularis L.): flowering stem with separate floral segments. Coloured etching by M. Bouchard, 177-.
creator: Unknown
attribution: Unknown, Granadilla or passion flower (Passiflora quadrangularis L.): flowering stem with separate floral segments. Coloured etching by M. Bouchard, 177-. . Wellcome Collection (Wellcome Collection), Public Domain Mark 1.0.
notes: Granadilla passion vine, long curling tendrils with leaves, flower and fruit, in a blue plate border. Hanging vine shape. Cutout moderate: border and caption to crop.

title: A clematis plant (Clematis cirrhosa): flowering stem. Coloured engraving by F. Sansom, c. 1807, after S. Edwards.
creator: Sydenham Edwards
attribution: Sydenham Edwards, A clematis plant (Clematis cirrhosa): flowering stem. Coloured engraving by F. Sansom, c. 1807, after S. Edwards. 1 December 1807. Wellcome Collection (Wellcome Collection), Public Domain Mark 1.0.
notes: Clematis cirrhosa, a drooping woody stem with cream bells; arching hanging shape. Cutout easy to moderate.

title: The male fern (Dryopteris filix-mas): fronds and part of rhizome. Colour nature print by A. Auer, c. 1853.
creator: Unknown
attribution: Unknown, The male fern (Dryopteris filix-mas): fronds and part of rhizome. Colour nature print by A. Auer, c. 1853. 1853 [1854]. Wellcome Collection (Wellcome Collection), Public Domain Mark 1.0.
notes: Male fern fronds and rhizome, nature print in green on aged paper with dark vignette. Great texture for a grotto curtain. Cutout moderate: toned mottled paper edge.

title: A fern frond, possibly of the male fern (Dryopteris filix-mas). Colour nature print, c. 1860.
creator: Unknown
attribution: Unknown, A fern frond, possibly of the male fern (Dryopteris filix-mas). Colour nature print, c. 1860. [c. 1860]. Wellcome Collection (Wellcome Collection), Public Domain Mark 1.0.
notes: A single fern frond with fine spore dots, blue-green on plain paper. Cutout easy; ideal repeating curtain element.

title: Ox-eye or marguerite daisy (Leucanthemum vulgare): flowers and leaves. Watercolour.
creator: Unknown
attribution: Unknown, Ox-eye or marguerite daisy (Leucanthemum vulgare): flowers and leaves. Watercolour. . Wellcome Collection (Wellcome Collection), Public Domain Mark 1.0.
notes: Ox-eye daisies in a loose bunch, hand-painted watercolour, white petals and yellow centres on aged paper. Cutout moderate (paper is stained).

title: Six grasses: fescues (Festuca species), foxtail grass (Alopecurus pratensis), meadow grasses (Poa species) and sweet vernal grass (Anthoxanthum odoratum). Coloured etching by J. Pass, c. 1807.
creator: Unknown
attribution: Unknown, Six grasses: fescues (Festuca species), foxtail grass (Alopecurus pratensis), meadow grasses (Poa species) and sweet vernal grass (Anthoxanthum odoratum). Coloured etching by J. Pass, c. 1807. 15 August 1807. Wellcome Collection (Wellcome Collection), Public Domain Mark 1.0.
notes: Six meadow grasses on one plate (fescues, foxtail, meadow grass) with seedheads and roots; blue-grey paper. Individual grasses separable. Cutout moderate (thin stems).

title: Meadow foxtail grass (Alopecurus pratensis): seedhead, leafy stems and floral segments. Coloured etching, c. 1805.
creator: Unknown
attribution: Unknown, Meadow foxtail grass (Alopecurus pratensis): seedhead, leafy stems and floral segments. Coloured etching, c. 1805. [1805]. Wellcome Collection (Wellcome Collection), Public Domain Mark 1.0.
notes: Meadow foxtail grass, one tall seedhead and leafy stems on blue-grey paper. Cutout moderate.

title: Six seeding plants, including dandelion, oak, sycamore and hazel, all illustrating different methods of seed dispersal. Chromolithograph, c. 1850.
creator: Unknown
attribution: Unknown, Six seeding plants, including dandelion, oak, sycamore and hazel, all illustrating different methods of seed dispersal. Chromolithograph, c. 1850. [1850?]. Wellcome Collection (Wellcome Collection), Public Domain Mark 1.0.
notes: Six seeding plants; top row has a round dandelion seed head (clock) with a leaf, plus a wheat ear. Round clock is small within the plate; crop required. Watercolour.

title: Dandelion (Taraxacum officinale): entire flowering plant. Coloured etching by C. Pierre, c. 1865, after P. Naudin.
creator: Naudin, Philibert, active 1870.
attribution: Naudin, Philibert, active 1870., Dandelion (Taraxacum officinale): entire flowering plant. Coloured etching by C. Pierre, c. 1865, after P. Naudin. [1865]. Wellcome Collection (Wellcome Collection), Public Domain Mark 1.0.
notes: Dandelion, entire plant with yellow flower and a closing seed head on the right, coloured etching. Seed head is small and partly shut, flower and rosette of leaves are the strong parts.

title: Les Roses: Rosa Longifolia
creator: Henri Joseph Redouté (French, 1766–1853)
attribution: Henri Joseph Redouté (French, 1766–1853), Les Roses:  Rosa Longifolia, 1817–1824. The Cleveland Museum of Art, Mr. and Mrs. Charles G. Prasse Collection (1965.294). CC0 1.0.
notes: Rosa longifolia, long slender cane with narrow leaves and pink open blooms, delicate. Cutout easy.

title: Les Roses: Rosa Candolleana Elegans
creator: Henri Joseph Redouté (French, 1766–1853)
attribution: Henri Joseph Redouté (French, 1766–1853), Les Roses:  Rosa Candolleana Elegans, 1817–1824. The Cleveland Museum of Art, Mr. and Mrs. Charles G. Prasse Collection (1965.295). CC0 1.0.
notes: Rosa candolleana elegans, rambling stem with many tiny leaflets and four white blooms with yellow centres, very graceful for a wall of ramblers. Cutout easy to moderate (fine leaflets).

title: Les Roses: Rosa alpina pendulina
creator: Henri Joseph Redouté (French, 1766–1853)
attribution: Henri Joseph Redouté (French, 1766–1853), Les Roses:  Rosa alpina pendulina, 1817–1824. The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of The Print Club of Cleveland in honor of Mrs. William G. Mather (1955.469). CC0 1.0.
notes: Rosa alpina pendulina, long arching cane with pointed leaflets, one crimson bloom and hip, on toned paper. Cutout easy.

title: [Dandelion Seeds]
creator: William Henry Fox Talbot
attribution: William Henry Fox Talbot, [Dandelion Seeds], 1858 or later. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Rogers Fund, 2004 (2004.111). CC0 1.0 (Open Access).
notes: Photogravure of a mass of dandelion seeds (pappus parachutes with seed bodies), black ink on cream paper. Not a clock but ideal drifting seeds layer after a luminance key and invert; dense, so crop or cut single parachutes. Cutout moderate (luminance key).

title: Damask rose (Rosa damascena "Italica"): flowering stem. Colour halftone after Victor, c.1824, after P. J. Redouté.
creator: Pierre-Joseph Redouté
attribution: Pierre-Joseph Redouté, Damask rose (Rosa damascena "Italica"): flowering stem. Colour halftone after Victor, c.1824, after P. J. Redouté. [1824]. Wellcome Collection (Wellcome Collection), Public Domain Mark 1.0.
notes: Blush Damask rose (Redoute plate, Les Quatre Saisons d'Italie): two tight buds, one half-open and a full double bloom on one stem, soft pink. Also usable as a hero blush rose. Colour halftone after the original; cutout easy on cream paper.

title: Red poppy (Papaver rhoeas): entire flowering plant. Coloured etching by C. Pierre, c. 1865, after P. Naudin.
creator: Naudin, Philibert, active 1870.
attribution: Naudin, Philibert, active 1870., Red poppy (Papaver rhoeas): entire flowering plant. Coloured etching by C. Pierre, c. 1865, after P. Naudin. [1865]. Wellcome Collection (Wellcome Collection), Public Domain Mark 1.0.
notes: Red poppy, entire plant with open red bloom, buds and root, coloured etching on pale grey paper. Strong colour, easy cutout; poppy is a small meadow flower for foreground.

title: Two types of buttercup (Ranunculus species): entire flowering plants. Coloured etching by C. Pierre, c. 1865, after P. Naudin.
creator: Naudin, Philibert, active 1870.
attribution: Naudin, Philibert, active 1870., Two types of buttercup (Ranunculus species): entire flowering plants. Coloured etching by C. Pierre, c. 1865, after P. Naudin. [1865]. Wellcome Collection (Wellcome Collection), Public Domain Mark 1.0.
notes: Two buttercups (meadow and creeping) with golden flowers, wavy leaves and roots, coloured etching on pale paper. Two plants separable. Cutout easy.

title: Fig. 1. Rosa semper virens - Rosier toujours vert. Fig. 2. Rosa bracteata - rosier a bractees (Ever-green rose - Macartney rose)
creator: Pierre-Joseph Redouté (figures), for Nouveau Duhamel (Veillard, Jaume Saint-Hilaire, Mirbel, Poiret, Loiseleur-Deslongchamps)
institution: The New York Public Library (via Wikimedia Commons)
attribution: Pierre-Joseph Redouté (figures), for Nouveau Duhamel (Veillard, Jaume Saint-Hilaire, Mirbel, Poiret, Loiseleur-Deslongchamps), Fig. 1. Rosa semper virens - Rosier toujours vert. Fig. 2. Rosa bracteata - rosier a bractees (Ever-green rose - Macartney rose), 1801. Wikimedia Commons, public domain. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Fig._1._Rosa_semper_virens_-_Rosier_toujours_vert._Fig._2._Rosa_bracteata_-_rosier_%C3%A0_bract%C3%A9es._(Ever-green_rose_-_Macartney_rose)_(NYPL_b14485031-1110809).tiff
notes: Evergreen rambler (Rosa sempervirens) with white blooms and small glossy leaflets above, Macartney rose (R. bracteata) below, on long trailing canes; coloured plate after Redoute, 1801. Scan includes a dark book edge and caption, crop required. Cutout moderate, whites need care on pale paper.

title: Rosarum monographia, or, A botanical history of roses (plate)
creator: John Lindley
institution: Internet Archive Book Images (via Wikimedia Commons)
attribution: John Lindley, Rosarum monographia, or, A botanical history of roses (plate), 1820. Wikimedia Commons, public domain. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Rosarum_monographia,_or,_A_botanical_history_of_roses_-_to_which_is_added_an_appendix,_for_the_use_of_cultivators,_in_which_the_most_remarkable_garden_varieties_are_systematically_arranged,_with_(14766967585).jpg
notes: Lindley's Rosarum Monographia plate: pink tight bud, half-open bloom and a red hip on one glaucous stem with grey-green leaflets; hand-coloured engraving. Gives bud and half-open stages and a hip. Cutout moderate (cream paper, page number and caption top and bottom).

title: Plate 19, Bellis perennis, Conversations on Botany
creator: Sarah Mary Fitton and Elizabeth Fitton; engraved by Thomas Milton
institution: Digital Public Library of America / Wikimedia Commons
attribution: Sarah Mary Fitton and Elizabeth Fitton; engraved by Thomas Milton, Plate 19, Bellis perennis, Conversations on Botany, 1817. Wikimedia Commons, public domain. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Plate_19-_Bellis_perennis_-_DPLA_-_615f2359d47d5c360df3eb01835f7ccd.jpg
notes: Common daisy (Bellis perennis) with fine root, rosette of leaves and florets dissected below; hand-coloured engraving, 1817. Pale pink-tipped daisy with yellow eye. Text from the opposite page ghosts through the paper, which needs cleaning; cutout moderate.

title: Ferns of Great Britain and Ireland: Polypodium Phegopteris
creator: Henry Bradbury (British, 1829–1860)
attribution: Henry Bradbury (British, 1829–1860), Ferns of Great Britain and Ireland:  Polypodium Phegopteris, 1855–1856. The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Robert Hershkowitz in honor of Evan H. Turner (1993.45). CC0 1.0.
notes: Nature-printed fern (Polypodium phegopteris, beech fern) in soft green with fine root mat, on clean white paper; Bradbury nature print from Moore's Ferns of Great Britain and Ireland. Cutout easy (paper key), fine roots are delicate. Ideal repeating curtain element.

title: Rosa multiflora - rosier multiflore (Rambler Rose, Multiflowered Rose)
creator: Pierre-Joseph Redouté (figures), for Nouveau Duhamel (Veillard, Jaume Saint-Hilaire, Mirbel, Poiret, Loiseleur-Deslongchamps)
attribution: Pierre-Joseph Redouté (figures), for Nouveau Duhamel (Veillard, Jaume Saint-Hilaire, Mirbel, Poiret, Loiseleur-Deslongchamps), Rosa multiflora - rosier multiflore (Rambler Rose, Multiflowered Rose), 1801. Wikimedia Commons, licensed Public domain (). Changes made: cut out and recoloured. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Rosa_multiflora_-_rosier_multiflore._(Rambler_Rose,_Multiflowered_Rose)_(NYPL_b14485031-1110813).tiff
notes: Rosa multiflora, the rambler rose: an arching cane with clusters of small pink double blooms, leaves and buds, plate after Redoute, 1801. Gravity-curved stem is ideal for a rose wall. Scan includes dark book edge and caption, crop required. Cutout moderate.

title: Hattersdorf Löwenzahn Samenstand-20180506-RM-184355
creator: Ermell
attribution: Ermell, Hattersdorf Löwenzahn Samenstand-20180506-RM-184355, 2018-05-06. Wikimedia Commons, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0). notes: Photograph of a perfectly round dandelion clock, silvery pappus against a black background, stem below, two soft out-of-focus clocks behind.
